title: Derivatives and small-step updates
summary: A derivative describes how a quantity changes per small change of its input. If $f(x)=x^2$, changing x from 2 to 2.01 changes f from 4 to 4.0401. The ratio is 0.0401/0.01=4.01. As the change shrinks, the ratio approaches 4, written $f'(2)=4$. The prime marks a derivative; it does not mean a different function chosen arbitrarily.

title: Positive semidefinite matrices
summary: A Hermitian matrix M is positive semidefinite when $v^\dagger Mv\ge0$ for every vector v. The dagger means [conjugate transpose](/definitions/conjugate-transpose/). For $M=\operatorname{diag}(2,0)$ and $v=(a,b)^T$, the expression is $2|a|^2$, never negative. Zero eigenvalues are allowed; “positive definite” requires strict positivity for every nonzero v.
